analysis.title: 'The Great Halving' Of Earnings Growth Ahead: Goldman's 2027 Equity Outlook Sees Value Now Hiding In Growth
key_insights: Goldman's 2027 global equity outlook (Oppenheimer) argues the AI capex boom is about to peak and global earnings growth will roughly halve, yet investors should return to long-duration Growth, starting with US hyperscalers.

US hyperscalers trade on 19.7x forward earnings, below their prior 20-year range and below Consumer Staples at 21.0x. Goldman calls them relatively defensive because net debt/equity remains healthy even though cash flow has turned negative.
Goldman sees the S&P 500 at 8,700 in 12 months (+14%), matching US strategist Ben Snider's target. The biggest upside is in TOPIX and Asia, and Europe is lowest at 6%.
Earnings growth is forecast to at least halve in nearly every major market in 2027: S&P 36% to 11%, STOXX 600 18% to 7%, TOPIX 24% to 9%, Asia from close to 80% to under 30%.
Goldman estimates hyperscaler capex added 12pp to S&P EPS growth in 2026 (5pp in 2025, 2pp in 2024). The contribution fades to 9pp in 2027 as depreciation bites and becomes a 5pp drag in 2028.

Consensus sector growth in 2027: IT slows from close to 90% to 45%, Communication Services from +34% to -5%, Energy from +99% to about -10%, Materials from 45% to 12%. Healthcare is the only sector expected to accelerate.
Goldman says the slowdown is relatively good for US hyperscalers, whose valuations have fallen, but raises more risk for chip names and Industrial cyclicals.
The Value vs Growth valuation gap has collapsed from above 100% at the 2021 peak to roughly 45-50%. Value is near the 90th percentile of its 20-year range and global tech is at the 20th percentile.
The valuation premium of the top 5 US stocks over the other 495 has virtually closed, far below the 2000 and 2021 peaks.

Korea's memory sector is pricing in a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, which Goldman's Asia strategists call excessive given disclosures of DRAM and HBM sold out until 2029. It trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B.

EM concentration is at a record: Korea and Taiwan are about half of MSCI EM, Info Tech is above 40%, and TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix are about 30%. EM's P/E discount to DM is about 50%, the widest since at least 2010.
Goldman forecasts the highest returns in Asia (17% USD price return for MXAPJ, 12% ex Korea and Taiwan) but stays neutral on a volatility-adjusted basis given 24.2% annualized vol.

Goldman's third theme is selective beneficiaries of lower oil and yields. Commodities see Brent falling from about $100 at end-2026 to $78 by end-2027, and Goldman expects the Fed and ECB to move toward cuts in late 2027.

The article notes the bond market is moving the other way: the 10Y is at 5.12% after a second consecutive hot CPI print, and Goldman's economists added a rate hike with cuts starting only in December 2027.

Regional stance: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe. Europe is hurt by Energy earnings exposure under lower oil, smaller valuation declines, government debt issues and a heavy political calendar.

Goldman lists four two-sided risks: bond volatility, oil, weaker AI capex and narrow breadth. It judges large-cap US tech more defensive than Asian tech, so momentum and concentration risk is higher in Asia.

The article challenges the defensive label. Hyperscalers burned $31B in Q3, issued $296B of debt this year against a $250B forecast, and have about $740B more queued for 2027. Consensus sees the group's FCF deficit deepening in 2027.

Market context: the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and the SOX 12% on Thursday, a basket of chip CDS traded wider than hyperscaler CDS for the first time, and Nvidia fell as much as 14% before dip buyers stepped in.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman prefers large-capex US hyperscalers as the defensive part of the Growth trade at 19.7x forward earnings, citing strong balance sheets and diversified income. The article disputes the defensive label because of negative free cash flow and heavy debt issuance.

Nvidia fell as much as 14% on Thursday after losing its chairman days before earnings, then recovered some of the drop as dip buyers stepped in. This is the article's market color, not a Goldman rating.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations have fallen, balance sheets are healthy on net debt/equity, and Goldman calls the group relatively defensive.
Large upside in memory and chips after de-rating, but Goldman flags much higher risk and volatility as capex growth slows.
The US ROE advantage keeps widening while its P/B premium has contracted.
Highest forecast returns but neutral on a volatility-adjusted basis, with record concentration in Korea and Taiwan.
Lower oil hurts earnings, valuations have not fallen as much, and sovereign debt and political risks are higher.
Only sector where consensus expects earnings growth to accelerate in 2027, and it has already re-rated.

earnings_insights: Goldman forecast S&P 500 EPS growth slows from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. STOXX 600 18% to 7%, TOPIX 24% to 9%, Asia from close to 80% to under 30%. These are Goldman forecasts, not reported figures.
Consensus (Street) expects 2027 IT earnings growth of 45% versus close to 90% in 2026, Communication Services -5% versus +34%, Energy about -10% versus +99%, Materials 12% versus 45%.
Goldman estimates hyperscaler capex contributed 12pp to S&P EPS growth in 2026, forecast at 9pp in 2027 and a 5pp drag in 2028.
Goldman's Asia strategists say Korea's memory sector is pricing in a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday (per the article).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields rose on Thursday after a second consecutive hot CPI print, which works against a long-duration Growth trade that needs lower yields.

macro_indicators.reading: second consecutive hot print, figure not given
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hot inflation pushed Treasuries lower and supports the Fed hiking for several more months.
Brent rebounded 3.3% on Thursday after Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran.
Goldman commodities expects Persian Gulf supply to recover, turning the energy shock from a 0.4pp drag on global growth into a modest tailwind.

macro_indicators.reading: rate cuts in late 2027, Goldman economists see cuts starting December 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman's rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing, but its economists recently added a rate hike, so the Fed is still hiking for about four more months.
Matches the target set by US strategist Ben Snider last month.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US hyperscalers as the defensive part of a long-duration Growth trade, after the de-rating to 19.7x forward earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuations are below their prior 20-year range and cheaper than Consumer Staples, with strong balance sheets and diversified income.
trade_ideas.risk: Capex slowing sharply, yields not falling while the Fed hikes, oil not normalizing, and the 2028 free cash flow rebound failing to arrive.

trade_ideas.description: Selectively add exposure to cyclical growth in memory and chips, especially Korea's memory sector
trade_ideas.rationale: Korea memory prices in a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings despite sold-out DRAM and HBM until 2029, and trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B.
trade_ideas.risk: Much higher risk and volatility, record EM concentration, and more exposure to the capex slowdown.

trade_ideas.description: Regional allocation: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: US ROE advantage is widening while its P/B premium has contracted, and Europe faces earnings and political risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Bond volatility, oil, weaker AI capex and narrow breadth.

risk_factors: Bond volatility, with sovereign debt risks highest in Europe in an election-heavy year.
Oil price swings and the Middle East outlook.
Weaker AI capex, with depreciation turning hyperscaler capex into an EPS drag in 2028.
Narrow market breadth and concentration, higher in Asia than in the US.
Hyperscaler free cash flow deficit deepening in 2027 while debt issuance reaches about $740B.
Credit spreads expected to widen by Goldman's credit strategists.
Nvidia leadership change days before its Tuesday earnings.
charts_described: Chart of 12-month forward EPS contribution versus multiple change in Asia ex-Japan and EM: EPS contributed roughly 70% while multiple compression took away more than 50% (read off the chart, approximate).
Chart of Value versus Growth valuation gap: collapsed from above 100% at the 2021 peak to roughly 45-50% (read off the chart).
Chart of hyperscaler capex contribution to S&P EPS growth: 2pp in 2024, 5pp in 2025, 12pp in 2026, 9pp in 2027 and a 5pp drag in 2028.
Chart showing Hardware and IT equipment trading at a discount to world ex-TMT for the first time since roughly 2019.
vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and the SOX 12% on Thursday, the Nasdaq 100's worst day since Covid per the article's opening.
The prior week the Nasdaq outperformed the SOX by nearly 460bps in one session, a top 10 daily spread in 10+ years per Goldman's Peter Callahan.
A basket of chip CDS traded wider than hyperscaler CDS for the first time this week.
The valuation premium of the top 5 US stocks over the other 495 has virtually closed.
EM concentration is at record highs, with the AI trio of TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix around 30% of MSCI EM.
Hardware and IT equipment trades at a discount to world ex-TMT for the first time since roughly 2019.
MXAPJ annualized volatility is 24.2%, which is why Goldman stays neutral on Asia despite the highest forecast return.
geopolitical: Iran war drove a 99% energy earnings gain this year and lifted oil, with Brent about $96 after Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran.
Goldman's lower oil view depends on Persian Gulf supply recovering and a 'normalisation in the Middle East', which the article calls a forecast.
Europe faces government debt issues and a heavy political calendar, with sovereign debt risks highest in Europe during an election-heavy year. The article hints at the French OAT market.
Fading tariff effects are cited as helping the Fed and ECB move toward cuts.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's 8,700 S&P target matches the one set by US strategist Ben Snider last month.
Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson warned in late October that semis could fall another 10-15% into mid-November.
Goldman's economists moved toward a rate hike, opposite to the strategists' lower-yield call.
Goldman credit strategists expect credit spreads to widen.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says hyperscalers at 19.7x forward earnings are cheaper than Consumer Staples, with healthy net debt/equity and diversified income. A capex slowdown is relatively good for them while it hurts chips and Industrial cyclicals.
tension_points.bear_case: The article says cash flow has turned negative with $31B burned in Q3, $296B of debt issued this year and about $740B queued for 2027. Consensus sees the FCF deficit deepening in 2027, and off-balance-sheet leases are not counted.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The article says the market could start pricing the debt, with credit spreads widening on $740 billion of 2027 AI issuance, or the 2028 free cash flow rebound failing to arrive on schedule.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing, with Brent falling to $78 and fading tariff effects letting the Fed and ECB cut in late 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10Y is at 5.12% after a second hot CPI print, and Goldman's own economists added a rate hike, with the Fed still hiking for about four more months and cuts only from December 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Long-duration Growth fails if yields keep rising while the Fed hikes, or if oil does not normalize because the US walks away from Iran talks.
